title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the preceding pages build the Gauss–Manin connection in the Katz–Oda manner. Take morphisms X --f--> S --> T with X smooth over S. The exact sequence (1), 0 → f*Ω¹_{S/T} → Ω¹_{X/T} → Ω¹_{X/S} → 0, splits locally. It induces the Koszul ('Leray') filtration F^p on Ω•_{X/T}, with graded pieces Gr^p ≃ f*Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗ Ω•_{X/S}[-p]. Pushing forward with Rf_* and using the projection formula gives Gr^p Rf_*Ω•_{X/T} ≃ Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗^L Rf_*Ω•_{X/S}[-p] (formula (3)). The connecting maps give the Gauss–Manin connection, and the spectral sequence of the filtered object gives a Leray-type spectral sequence. The previous page also interprets classes in E_∞^{1,n-1} as torsors with a 'derivation' d_P.

This page, 'Variantes':

(a) Coefficients. Replace O_X by a quasi-coherent E on X with an integrable connection relative to T. Then Ω•_{X/T}⊗E is a complex, the de Rham complex of (E,∇).
- Because (1) splits locally, the filtration tensors correctly: Gr^p_{X/S}(Ω•_{X/T}⊗E) ≃ Gr^p_{X/S}(Ω•_{X/T})⊗E. This is a priori only an additive (not O-linear complex) identification, since the differentials are only f^{-1}O_S-linear.
- Using the projection formula as in (3), formula (21) states: Gr^p(Rf_*(Ω•_{X/T}⊗E)) ≃ Ω^p_{S/T} ⊗^L Rf_*(Ω•_{X/S}⊗E)[-p].
- Grothendieck says it seems sufficient that E be flat over X and Ω¹_{S/T} be flat over S. Under this proviso one gets integrable (Gauss–Manin) connections on the relative de Rham cohomology R^q f_*(Ω•_{X/S}⊗E) relative to T.
- One also gets a spectral sequence. When Ω¹_{S/T} is flat it takes the form (22): E_2^{pq} = H^p_DR(S/T, H^q_DR(X/S,E)) ⇒ H^*_DR(X/T,E). Here the coefficient system H^q_DR(X/S,E) carries its Gauss–Manin connection.

(b) Base change of the picture. The spectral sequence can be localized over T. More generally, given any further morphism S → R (or T → base), one expects compatibility of the spectral sequence with the integrable connections relative to a base over which T lies. In other words, the Leray spectral sequence of de Rham cohomology is itself horizontal for a 'higher' Gauss–Manin connection.

The page is a sketch of the coefficient version of the Katz–Oda construction and of the de Rham Leray spectral sequence. The next page starts a new section on the Cartier operation.
errors: The hedge 'il semble qu'il suffise que E plat sur X' is probably more than needed. Because (1) splits locally, Gr^p ≃ f*Ω^p_{S/T}⊗Ω•_{X/S}⊗E holds for any quasi-coherent E. The projection formula for quasi-coherent sheaves (f qcqs) does not require E flat. Flatness (local freeness) of Ω¹_{S/T} is what is needed to remove the derived tensor and identify E_1/E_2 with de Rham complexes of the Gauss–Manin system.
Implicit hypotheses are not stated on the page: X smooth over S (needed for (1) to be locally split exact), and f quasi-compact and quasi-separated.

The Gr identification is only additive, i.e. f^{-1}O_S-linear rather than O_X-linear. Grothendieck notes this himself, but the use of the projection formula for complexes with non-O_X-linear differentials needs the standard care (e.g. working termwise or filtering further), as in Katz–Oda.

ideas.what: Gauss–Manin connection with coefficients in a module with integrable connection, via the Koszul filtration of Ω•_{X/T}⊗E
ideas.modern_name: Gauss–Manin connection on relative de Rham cohomology with coefficients (Katz–Oda construction)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Katz–Oda (1968); Katz, 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' (1970), §3

ideas.what: Leray spectral sequence E_2^{pq}=H^p_DR(S/T, H^q_DR(X/S,E)) ⇒ H^*_DR(X/T,E)
ideas.modern_name: Leray spectral sequence for algebraic de Rham cohomology / Katz–Oda spectral sequence

ideas.what: Projection-formula identification Gr^p Rf_*(Ω•_{X/T}⊗E) ≃ Ω^p_{S/T}⊗^L Rf_*(Ω•_{X/S}⊗E)[-p], without flatness and hence with derived tensor
ideas.modern_name: Graded pieces of the Koszul filtration under derived pushforward

ideas.what: Compatibility of the Leray spectral sequence with Gauss–Manin connections relative to a further base (localizing over T / over S→R)
ideas.modern_name: Horizontality of the Leray spectral sequence for Gauss–Manin connections
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; implicit in Katz–Oda and later work on variations of mixed structures

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine variant (coefficients, base change) of the Katz–Oda construction and its Leray spectral sequence, both well established in the literature since 1968–70. The only minor points are the derived-tensor formulation without flatness of Ω¹_{S/T} and the hedged flatness conditions, neither of which would surprise a specialist.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'un module de coh. quasi-coh.' is likely just 'un module quasi-coh[érent]'. A symbol (X) is crossed out before it.
'est un point de vue additif' should probably read 'est un iso additif' (an additive isomorphism, not one of O-module complexes).
'Pour pouvoir expliquer en point de vue (3)' is more plausibly 'Pour pouvoir appliquer ce qui précède [à] (3)', with a marginal reference '(3)'.
'il semble qu'il [-faille-] suffise[?]': 'faille' is struck through. The phrases 'E plat sur X' and 'plat sur S' are underlined in the manuscript.
'faisceaux[?]' is preceded by a struck word; the intended phrase is 'connexions intégrables sur les [faisceaux] Rf_*(Ω•_{X/S}⊗E) rel. à T'.

In (b) the struck text reads something like 'formules des' before 'S → R'. The last lines read 'compatibilités de la suite spectrale obtenue sur T, avec des connexions intégrables relativement à une base au-dessus de T'.
